output.title: Synthetic test data is a tool, not the point
output.body:
Synthetic test data is useful when it helps you answer a bounded workflow question faster. It is less useful when it turns into a project of its own. If you run a small business, the real question is simple: are you building fake records because you need privacy or scale, or because nobody has tried the workflow on real records yet?

For a repeatable task like invoice handling or customer inquiry triage, I would usually start smaller: a limited real-data subset, clear rules, and a human approval step where money or another high-risk decision is involved. That keeps the test focused on the workflow, not on polishing data that never shows up in production.

Bareni’s own accounts-payable demo is a useful boundary case. It uses entirely synthetic data to show the mechanics: text-based invoice extraction, arithmetic checks, duplicate blocking, and audit records. But the limits matter too. The default route uses pre-extracted files, and PDF/scan ingestion plus OCR are not implemented. So the demo shows control logic; it is not a claim that every real invoice stack is ready.

My practical next step would be to pick one workflow, one approval rule, and one small batch of real records. Then ask whether synthetic data is solving a real testing problem, or just delaying the moment you learn what the workflow actually needs.】【。
